Illinois High School SGP Calculation
Implications of the transition from SAT to ACT
Damian Betebenner & Adam VanIwaarden
Center for Assessment

June 17th, 2025

Transition from SAT to ACT
• Beginning in spring 2025, in grades 9, 10 and 11, Illinois
 transitioned from the SAT suite of assessments (PSAT9, PSAT, SAT)
 to the ACT suite of assessments (PreACT9, PreACT, ACT).
• The SAT and ACT suite of assessments test students in ELA and
 Mathematics
• Students will continue to take the IAR in grades 3 to 8 for ELA and
 Mathematics.
• The question addressed is whether there will be any interruption
 or impact to SGP analyses from the transition.

SGP: Scale agnosticism
• SGPs, being norm-referenced, are, in general, immune to assessment transitions:
 • As long as all students take the “same” assessment at the “same” time, we can calculate
 growth-norms associated with those students.
 • NOTE: SGPs referred to here are cohort-referenced and not baseline-referenced.
• In addition, the analytic methodology behind SGP calculation is designed to be invariant to
 mono-tone transformations of scale.
 • In theory, if there is a mono-tone transformation of scale between two assessments, then
 SGPs will be invariant to that transformation.
• SGPs have been successfully calculated across numerous assessment transitions (state transition
 to PARCC and SBAC, for example)

Other Concerns
• Despite superior analytic properties and a history of successful
 assessment transitions, one concern about the transition from
 the College Board to ACT suite of assessments has to do with
 scale granularity.
• By granularity we mean the number and distribution of scale
 score outcomes realizable by the given assessment.
• SGP calculations require sufficient scale granularity in order to
 calculate the 99 conditional quantile curves associated with the
 multivariate test data.

Score Granularity
• College Board Assessments:
 • SAT: Reported on a scale of 200 to 800 in multiples of 10.
 • PSAT: Reported on a scale of 160 to 760 in multiples of 10.
 • PSAT9: Reported on a scale of 120 to 720 in multiples of 10.
• ACT Assessments:
 • ACT: Reported on a scale of 1 to 36 in integers.
 • PreACT: Reported on a scale of 1 to 35 in integers.
 • PreACT9: Reported on a scale of 1 to 35 in integers.
• When examining scale score distributions, there are substantially fewer reported
 scale scores for the ACT suite of assessments than the SAT suite of assessments.

Implications
• Though there are several states that have run SGP analyses using ACT
 as the dependent variable (current assessment) with state assessment
 priors, no state we have worked with has calculated growth using ACT
 assessments both as current and prior assessments.
• There is a concern that the lack of scale granularity may lead to poor
 model fit and corrupt the intended uses for the SGPs.
• To provide guidance to Illinois as they transition to ACT assessments,
 we utilized historical Illinois SAT data combined with scale
 concordances from SAT to ACT to simulate what outcomes will look
 like for ACT assessments.

Data
• ISBE provided historical student data for both IAR grades 3 to
 8 and PAST9/PSAT/SAT.
 • Data was provided for both ELA and Mathematics
 • Data was provided for 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2024.
• For the purposes of these analyses we utilize 2022, 2023 and
 2024 data.
• Individual tested student counts range from approximately
 100,000 to 110,000 per grade

SAT to ACT Concordance
• SAT to ACT: Scores were converted to the ACT scale using the published, readily available
 concordance table: SAT Math to ACT Math and SAT ERW to ACT English + Reading.
 • For conversions from the lowest reported score in the concordance table to the
 LOSS, linear interpolation was used.
• PSAT to PreACT: Scores were converted using the concordance table where PSAT scores
 ranged from 160 to 760 and PreACT scores ranged from 1 to 35 with the same linear
 interpolation at the bottom of the scale.
• PSAT9 to PreACT9: Scores were converted using the concordance table where PSAT
 scores ranged from 120 to 720 and the PreACT9 scores were assumed to range from 1 to
 35.
• Though the latter two concordances are not “official”, they suffice for the investigation to
 see whether score granularity will be a problem with SGP calculation.

SGP Analyses
• With PSAT9, PSAT, and SAT scores converted to the ACT scale
 via the concordances, 3 analyses each in ELA and
 Mathematics were performed:
 • IAR7/2022, IAR8/2023, PreACT9/2024
 • IAR8/2022, PreACT9/2023, PreACT10/2024
 • PreACT9/2022, PreACT10/2023, ACT/2024
• NOTE: All references to ACT tests above refer to SAT scores
 translated to the ACT scale.

SGP Analyses
• All SGP analyses were conducted using the R software environment
 together with the SGP package (v2.2-1.9995).
• Knots and boundaries utilized for b-spline calculation were derived
 from the translated SAT scores for use in the calculations.
• Achievement level cuts associate with the ACT scores were derived
 via the cut-scores currently employed by Illinois for the SAT.
• All analyses executed without error providing SGP results for all
 students with suitable longitudinal scale scores.
• Goodness of fit plots are shown on the next several pages.

Conclusions
• Despite the coarseness of the ACT scale, the SGP analyses featured very
 good fit.
• Any misfit shown in the data would what compensated for by adjacent cells
 in the goodness of fit plots suggesting the coarseness of the data making it
 impossible to subdivide a point mass of students at a particular scale score.
• The grade 10 ELA scores did show some evidence of a ceiling leading to
 students (likely with successive perfect scores) having low SGPs.
• Overall, based upon the results of this study we believe that Illinois will be
 able to calculate SGPs using ACT data with sufficient technical quality for
 use.
